summary.text: A 10-year-old girl was diagnosed with juvenile dermatomyositis based on progressive proximal weakness, polyarthritis, pathognomonic rashes, laboratory evidence of myositis, anti-TIF-1γ and anti-P155/140 antibodies, and thigh MRI showing symmetric myositis and mild subcutaneous edema. She started methotrexate and prednisone; strength and arthritis improved rapidly but her skin disease persisted.

Monthly IVIG was added for refractory dermatologic symptoms. A significant headache followed the first infusion and needed frequent analgesic medications, but her skin improved markedly, so IVIG continued at a slower infusion rate that she tolerated well. She was weaned off steroids 8 months after diagnosis.

After 8 months of IVIG therapy she developed an intractable headache lasting 9 days. MR brain imaging showed indications of elevated intracranial pressure, ophthalmology confirmed bilateral optic disc edema, and lumbar puncture showed an elevated opening pressure of 36 cm H2O with a closing pressure of 32 cm H2O.

A Diamox taper was started and IVIG was discontinued. Follow-up imaging 2 months later indicated resolution of the elevated ICP. She subsequently maintained remission with methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine; the source wording on recurrence of elevated ICP is ambiguous.

summary.text: A 7-year-old girl with progressive proximal muscle weakness and rash was diagnosed with juvenile dermatomyositis with positive TIF-1γ antibodies. She started prednisone and methotrexate, but her skin remained refractory with persistent elevations in muscle enzymes and inflammatory markers.

Monthly IVIG was started with acetaminophen, diphenhydramine and methylprednisolone premedication. Her symptoms improved significantly and muscle enzyme levels returned to normal, although she developed intermittent nausea and headaches after infusions.

Six months after starting IVIG an ophthalmology examination revealed elevated ICP and glaucoma. Steroids were tapered, but bilateral papilledema progressed from grade 2 to grade 3 and then grade 4. MR imaging showed left frontal sulcal signal loss indicative of superficial siderosis and arterial irregularity raising concern for vasculitis; lumbar punctures showed opening pressures of 45 and 49 cm H2O with unremarkable CSF, and Lyme disease, thyroid dysfunction and vitamin A and D toxicity were ruled out.

IVIG was gradually tapered off over 2 months after 11 doses, with a transition to mycophenolate mofetil decided. About 2 months after discontinuing IVIG there was near-complete resolution of optic disc edema and elevated ICP, and imaging 4 months after discontinuation showed no new siderosis, normalized cerebral arteries and no papilledema.
